title: Massive haematemesis with a clean endoscopy

source.citation: Wiesmueller F, Neufert C, Siebler J, Croner R, Lang W, Grützmann R. Primary aortoduodenal fistula - overlooked because of guidelines? Innov Surg Sci. 2020;5(3-4):133-136.

presentation.hpi: Transferred from another hospital because of heavy upper gastrointestinal bleeding. Known arterial hypertension; history of alcohol abuse and nicotine dependence.
presentation.social: History of alcohol abuse; nicotine dependence

exam: Pale and in severe distress; otherwise unremarkable examination
SpO2 100% on 2 L/min oxygen by nasal cannula

imaging.finding: Infrarenal aorta not visible because of excessive bowel gas
Large blood clots in the stomach; no active bleeding source in the stomach or duodenum
Small gastric erosion, clipped; no other source of bleeding
Blood clots in the colon; no source of bleeding
Several ulcers and pulsatile bleeding in the distal duodenum; massive intraluminal blood obscured the exact site

diagnosis.primary: Primary aortoduodenal fistula from a 5.5 cm abdominal aortic aneurysm adherent to the third part of the duodenum, presenting with a herald bleed
differentials: Bleeding peptic ulcer (posterior duodenal bulb, gastroduodenal artery)

management: Immediate treatment of haemorrhagic shock: large-volume IV infusions, transfusions and multiple vasopressors
Emergency upper endoscopy (no source), then high-dose IV proton-pump inhibitor and IV erythromycin
Acute kidney injury treated with continuous haemofiltration
Day 2: clip to a small gastric erosion; colonoscopy after recurrent hypotension and haematochezia, without a source
Three bleed-free days followed; the scheduled CT was postponed because he had improved
Day 5: sudden haematemesis and cardiac arrest during emergency endoscopy; CPR
Emergency laparotomy under continuous CPR: fistula excised and a 24 mm polyester aortic inlay graft placed
Months of intensive care and repeated surgery; 173 units of red cells, 118 units of plasma and 25 platelet transfusions
outcome: Multiple organ dysfunction despite months of intensive care; treatment was limited to palliative care and he died on day 122.
teachingPoints: A herald bleed (a self-limited, sometimes massive bleed followed by a bleed-free interval of hours to months) often precedes exsanguination from an aortoenteric fistula.
The fistula usually involves the third or fourth part of the duodenum, beyond the usual reach of upper endoscopy, so a negative EGD does not exclude it.
In massive or obscure upper GI bleeding with a non-diagnostic endoscopy, obtain CT angiography early; bedside ultrasound often cannot show the aorta.
Primary fistulas arise from an aortic aneurysm; secondary fistulas (more common) follow aortic graft repair, so any GI bleed after aortic surgery is a fistula until proven otherwise.
Untreated mortality approaches 100%; definitive care is aortic repair (open, or endovascular as a bridge) with management of the bowel defect and infection.

questions.q: What is the most appropriate next investigation?
questions.extra: Hb 3 g/dL. Nasogastric tube drains fresh red blood. Emergency EGD: large gastric clots, no active bleeding source in the stomach or duodenum. Bedside ultrasound could not see the infrarenal aorta (bowel gas).
options: Repeat upper endoscopy in 24 hours on a PPI infusion
CT angiography of the abdomen and pelvis now
questions.explanation: Life-threatening bleeding with a non-diagnostic endoscopy calls for CT angiography: it localises active bleeding and shows the aorta, which ultrasound could not. Scintigraphy is too slow for an unstable patient, and waiting for repeat endoscopy (as happened here, after a bleed-free interval) let the fistula declare itself by exsanguination.

questions.q: What is the most likely source of the bleeding?
questions.extra: After three bleed-free days, sudden massive haematemesis on day 5. Emergency EGD: several ulcers and pulsatile bleeding in the distal duodenum; he arrests during the procedure.
options: Posterior duodenal bulb ulcer eroding the gastroduodenal artery
Oesophageal variceal rupture from alcohol-related cirrhosis
Dieulafoy lesion of the gastric fundus missed at endoscopy
Abdominal aortic aneurysm eroding into the distal duodenum
questions.explanation: A massive bleed that stopped on its own and returned as exsanguination after a bleed-free interval (a herald bleed), from the distal duodenum that lies on the infrarenal aorta, is the pattern of an aortoenteric fistula; laparotomy found a 5.5 cm aneurysm adherent to D3. The duodenal bulb and fundus had been seen without a source.

questions.extra: Laparotomy: a 5.5 cm abdominal aortic aneurysm adherent to the third part of the duodenum, with a fistula between them.
options: Endoscopic clipping and adrenaline injection at the bleeding point
Transcatheter embolisation of the gastroduodenal artery
Excision of the fistula, aortic graft repair and duodenal closure
Duodenotomy with under-running of a bleeding duodenal ulcer
questions.explanation: Only aortic repair closes the communication: excision of the fistula with graft replacement (in situ or extra-anatomic) and duodenal repair, or endovascular repair as a bridge in unstable patients, with antibiotic cover. Untreated mortality approaches 100%; endoscopic, embolic or ulcer surgery treats the wrong vessel.

evidence.quote: A 63 year-old man was transferred to our emergency department for significant gastrointestinal bleeding.
a 63 year-old male who exhibited significant upper gastrointestinal bleeding and hemorrhagic shock
Upon arrival, the patient was awake but not oriented.
a respiratory rate of 40/min, a pulse of 121 beats/min, a blood pressure of 105/38 mmHg
100% oxygen saturation at 2 L/min per nasal cannula
Physical examination showed a pale appearing male in severe distress but was otherwise unremarkable.
A complete blood count revealed a hemoglobin concentration of 3 g/dL.
His medical history included arterial hypertension, alcohol abuse and nicotine dependence.
Treatment for hemorrhagic shock was initiated immediately by administering large intravenous volume infusions, transfusions and multiple vasopressors.
A focused assessment with sonography for trauma scan was performed. However, the infrarenal part of aorta was not visible due to excessive bowel gas.
The patient was intubated and a nasogastric tube was placed which revealed fresh red blood.
An emergency esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) was performed, which showed large blood clots in the stomach
an active source of bleeding was not present, neither in the stomach nor the duodenum
High-dose proton-pump inhibitors and erythromycin were infused intravenously.
the patient went into acute renal failure and required continuous hemofiltration
The next day, repeat EGD revealed a small gastric erosion which was supplied with a metal clip.
the patient suffered from repeat hypotension and hematochezia. A colonoscopy demonstrated blood clots in the colon but no source of bleeding.
For three days, he did not exhibit any signs of bleeding. A scheduled computed tomography (CT) scan was postponed due to improved condition of the patient.
after five days the patient suddenly developed hematemesis. During emergency EGD, the patient suffered cardiac arrest and required cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR).
The distal part of the duodenum exhibited several ulcers and a pulsatile bleeding. Intraluminal exsanguination was massive
The patient was transferred to the operating room under continuous CPR for emergency laparotomy.
An abdominal aortic aneurysm of 5.5 cm diameter adherent to the third part of the duodenum was appreciated.
Emergency laparotomy disclosed an aortoduodenal fistula.
The aortoduodenal fistula … was excised and an aortic 24 mm polyester graft was implanted in inlay technique
the hemorrhage-free interval after the herald bleed may have led to not insisting on immediate CT imaging
a total of 25 platelet transfusions, 118 units of fresh frozen plasma, and 173 units of packed red blood cells
Despite these efforts, multiple organ dysfunction evolved. Decision was made to limit treatment to palliative care
After 122 days, the patient succumbed to his condition.
